summary: A is closer to the frozen contract and substantially safer to merge, although it still needs revision to delegate Upload to Add and add the required tests. B provides stronger Upload tests but introduces an explicitly forbidden, risky refactor of generic request-body handling.
reasons: Both implementations incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing the multipart body through Add.
A preserves existing Add and retry machinery, keeping the change narrowly scoped to the convenience API and helper reuse.
B changes RawClient.Do semantics for every io.ReadSeeker, despite the contract explicitly prohibiting unrelated request/retry refactoring.

B’s GetBody returns the same mutable ReadSeeker after rewinding it, rather than a fresh body copy as GetBody conventionally promises; this creates redirect/concurrency hazards and changes reader-closing ownership globally visible to callers toward a model different from existing behavior, as its changelog acknowledges explicitly stating callers now own seekable bodies and the client no longer closes them.
